stories.summary: Police detained former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Jabra (also spelled Rana) from his Maharajgunj residence, acting on a complaint filed at the Valley Crime Investigation Office in Teku, according to police sources. Officials have not yet disclosed the nature of the complaint against him.

stories.headline: Nationwide floods and landslides from incessant rain kill six, disrupt roads and rivers across Nepal
stories.summary: Continuous monsoon rain has caused flooding and landslides across Nepal, with central police spokesperson Avinarayan Kafle confirming six deaths and 407 people rescued since Asoj 8; rivers including Narayani, Tinau, Lal Bakaiya, Saptakoshi and Kaligandaki have crossed or neared danger levels, flooding roughly 500 homes in Saptari and damaging houses in Butwal, Bardiya, Myagdi and Baglung, while highways including the East-West Highway and routes to Baglung, Solukhumbu and Jomsom-Korala are blocked. The Meteorological Department forecasts continued heavy rain in Gandaki, Lumbini, Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces, though eastern Nepal is expected to see improvement, as Humla recorded its heaviest rainfall in 46 years.

stories.headline: Nepali Army calls Bhotekoshi tunnel rescue in Rasuwa floods 'historic and unparalleled'
stories.summary: The Nepali Army has concluded that its role in managing the Rasuwa Bhotekoshi flood disaster was unparalleled, historic and exemplary, citing extreme risks including unpredictable weather, narrow mountainous flight corridors, limited helipads, blocked communication and debris-choked tunnels; the army says seven people were rescued alive from hydropower tunnels buried by flood debris. The report comes as Nepal Press notes the recovery from the month-old Bhotekoshi flood remains slow, with only some roads and bridges temporarily reconnected and relief for affected families still ongoing.

advocate.argument: This is the arrest of a former Chief Justice of Nepal's Supreme Court, one of the most senior judicial officials in the country's history, and it is confirmed independently by the Kathmandu Post (English), Ratopati, OnlineKhabar, Nagarik, Nepal Press, DC Nepal and Khabarhub. Rana already carries a public record: he faced an impeachment motion in Parliament in February 2022 that led to his suspension until his term ended in December 2022, making this arrest the latest chapter in a long-running institutional controversy over judicial accountability in Nepal. A sitting-level former head of the judiciary being taken from his home at night by the Valley Crime Investigation Office is a rare, high-status arrest that will dominate Nepali news cycles regardless of what the underlying complaint turns out to be. The story is easy to report accurately today because every fact in the summary — arrest location, arresting unit, absence of disclosed charges — is corroborated across multiple independent outlets, both Nepali and English.
